newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -T-BONDS TO BREAK DOWN TOWARDS 113-03.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -T-BONDS TO BREAK DOWN TOWARDS 113-03.

text.p: September T-bond futures will head lower on Friday towards the key 113-03 level, technical analysts said.
On the way down, Tom Hobson, manager of technical analysis at Merrill Lynch in London said the market would look to support at 113-24, the current level from a 2-1/2 month trendline.
"That should hold initially, but a break there would send the contract down to its to most important support level, which is 113-03," he said.
A 61.8 percent Fibonacci retracement of the July rally and the low on July 7 coincide at 113-03.
At 0957 GMT, September T-bonds were at 113-31, down 8/32 in automated trade.
Hobson said the breakdown in Eurodollar contracts on Thursday indicated a more negative outlook towards futures short end interest rates next year and would cap the Treasury contracts.

"For T-bonds, the most important thing this week has been the inability to recover above initial resistance targets. That has indicated that the short-term directional risk is still to the downside," he said.
From an intermediate term standpoint, he said Thursday's failure at 115-06 would be the major resistance hurdle.
He also noted lower resistance around 114-10, 12 from previous consolidation.
Technical analysts at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London agreed T-bonds were likely to move lower.
"There is minor support near 114-03 but look for a rundown to 113-23/12 before a larger bounce is possible," they said in a research note.
"If this move remains impulsive, a move below key supports in the 112-24/19 becomes possible."

The DMG analysts said the rally to 115-06 could be interpreted as the fourth wave of an Elliott wave pattern, indicating more downside moves, but it could also be seen as a 'b' wave, suggesting the chance of new highs in the coming weeks.
December Eurodollar futures were at 94.055, down 0.015.
